text:
infra-bot: SLO_ALERT: hosted-infer-usw2 p99 latency > 3s and 5xx fraction > 2% (started 2026-03-17T09:54:00Z). linked alert: https://console.redwood/internal/alerts/8140001234 :rotating_light:

alex: seeing a 5xx spike and timeouts across the gateway. probe vs real traffic both impacted. customer support just flagged increased errors.

sam: jumping in — which zone? dashboard shows hotspots in us-west-2 and eu-west-1.

alex: primary visible in us-west-2. dashboards: https://console.redwood/dashboards/hosted-infer/gateway-5xx-wave

priya: traces are sparse — large trace gaps for the affected requests (many requests show no downstream spans). could be sampling or an injector failing.

kevin: support-bot pulled a few customer logs. one customer saw repeated 502s immediately after a token refresh event. support-bot: "customer-request-ids: [req_32fa, req_32fb, req_32fc]"

sam: low-hanging checks: 1) auth service logs around token rotation 2) rate-limiter 503s 3) prefetch/kvcache errors.

alex: ran a quick query (logs -> kusto):
```
logs
| where service == "proxy-gateway" and timestamp > ago(30m)
| where status_code >= 500
| summarize count() by status_code, upstream_service
| sort by count_ desc
```
Result: spike of 502s attributed to upstream "authz-ingress" returning 502/timeout.

priya: I see a correlated increase in handshakes failing to authz-ingress around the same window. grabbing the authz logs.

sam: can someone try a repro curl against the public hosted inference endpoint with a rotated token? include verbose so we can see handshake timings. e.g.
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <rotated_token>" \\n  -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
```
I tried and got HTTP/1.1 502 after 1.9s with no downstream span.

alex: copying response snippet from curl: "RIS: upstream reset during handshake" and gateway logs show TLS handshake timeouts to authz-ingress.

kevin: support-bot pulled billing events too — there was a billing microdeploy 10m before the spike. deploying rollback?

priya: if billing service called authz or token verifier as part of usage check, a deploy there could transiently slow authz path. checking service-deploy logs: deployment ID deploy_20260317_0950 by ops-release.

sam: putting hypothesis: billing deploy caused backpressure on shared authz backend which caused authz timeouts -> gateway returned 502s and traces dropped. need to confirm call graph.

alex: quick mitigation options: 1) increase gateway upstream timeout for authz-ingress to 5s temporarily 2) enable fallback auth (local cache) for known-good tokens 3) rollback billing deploy.

kevin: rolling back billing deploy now (started). I'll ping when complete.

priya: meanwhile adding a temporary alert rule to watch authz 5xx rate and Gateway p99 > 3s. I'll also open a short-lived suppression for noisy customer alerts.

sam: capturing trace query to find requests with missing downstream spans:
```
traces | where service == "gateway" and timestamp > ago(30m)
| where not(has_downstream_span) and http.status_code >= 500
| project trace_id, request_id, http.path, duration_ms
```
Share any trace_ids here so we can stitch logs.

alex: attaching 3 trace_ids from affected customer: trace_aa12, trace_bb34, trace_cc56.

priya: authz logs show repeated 504 gateway timeouts for those trace_ids. stack shows heavy GC pause on one authz instance and connection pool exhaustion on another.

kevin: rollback finished — deploy_20260317_0950 -> reverted at 2026-03-17T10:02:00Z.

infra-bot: DEPLOY_ROLLBACK: deploy_20260317_0950 reverted by kevin at 2026-03-17T10:02:00Z.

sam: post-rollback metrics: 5xx fraction dropping, p99 improving. still seeing some tail but much better.

alex: customers are reporting fewer errors now. recommend keeping increased timeout and local token cache for 20m while we stabilize.

priya: creating a follow-up runbook: investigate autoscaling config for authz, connection pool sizing, and add health endpoint checks before rollout. file: https://confluence.redwood/runbooks/authz-deploy-checks

kevin: opening inc ticket INC-20260317-007 and tagging infra release team + oncall. will include timeline, rollback, affected customers, and mitigation steps.

alex: next steps: (1) postmortem if we get > 30min of SLO burn (2) small change to add graceful degradation on billing->auth calls (3) run a deploy gating test that simulates token churn.

support-bot: Noted affected customers (cust_123, cust_456) informed via support ticket TKT-9981.

sam: thanks everyone. leaving this thread open until metrics stable for 30m. :white_check_mark:

kevin: ack, will follow up in the incident ticket with logs and trace links.

priya: adding final note: trace gaps were mostly due to gateway returning early 502s before upstream got instrumented. improving instrumentation is on the short-term action list.

alex: closing loop — metrics back to baseline at 2026-03-17T10:25:05Z. will flag for postmortem if support escalations continue. :relieved:
